title: Correcting for enzyme immunoassay changes in long term monitoring studies
author: Wilson, Sergiel, et al.

steps.title: Assemble full dataset
steps.instruction: Gather all hair cortisol concentration measurements obtained with enzyme immunoassay kit 1 and kit 2 for the brown bear samples collected in Sweden and Alberta (1996–2013).

steps.title: Create mixed population
steps.instruction: Combine every sample (both kits, all sexes) into a single dataset that will be used for model training and testing.

steps.title: Randomly split data
steps.instruction: Randomly assign two‑thirds of the total samples to a training group and the remaining one‑third to a test group.

steps.title: Fit linear regression models
steps.instruction: Using the training group, fit a simple linear regression (kit2 = a × kit1 + b) for (i) the whole mixed population, (ii) males only, and (iii) females only. Record the equations and R² values:

steps.title: Predict test‑set concentrations
steps.instruction: Apply each respective regression equation to the corresponding test‑set samples to obtain predicted kit 2 cortisol concentrations.

steps.title: Assess model performance
steps.instruction: For each dataset (all, males, females) evaluate the predictions using four metrics:

substeps.instruction: Calculate the percent of test samples that are over‑estimated and the percent that are under‑estimated.
Compute the mean predicted percent error (PE) = (|actual – predicted| / actual) × 100 and report mean ± SD.
Determine the percentage of samples with PE < 20 %.
Perform a Wilcoxon signed‑rank test comparing predicted versus actual concentrations; report median predicted, median actual, and p‑value.
